title: Leads backend core: create/list/get/update, tenant-formatted refs, duplicate checks, bulk reassign, breadth permissions
objective: Port the lead intake/edit and list/detail core: full-field New/Edit Lead per the implemented spec, system-generated tenant-formatted lead refs via transactional per-tenant/year sequences, non-blocking duplicate warnings, permission-bound bulk reassign with mandatory audit note, and visibility-breadth (view_all vs own) enforcement in query filters (P-06, P-08 core).
scope: POST /api/v1/leads (full validation catalog: party picker/inline new party, existing/new client, date received not future, channel with broker requirement, owner defaulting via rm slot, region defaulting from party, external ref uniqueness warning, product line -> cover type dependency, premium > 0 when provided, policy term incl. Other free-text required, derived-High priority, intake notes as first activity)

GET /api/v1/leads (implemented columns/filters/sort/paging/search, My-leads toggle honoring breadth permissions, aging/flag indicators data), GET /{id}, PUT /{id} (draft-editable fields per reference)
Lead ref generation: tenant format template + per-tenant/year reference_sequences allocation via SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside the create transaction (pooler-safe)
Status always New on creation; duplicate-lead warning non-blocking
implementation_details: Port the FluentValidation lead validators to zod verbatim (section 14 catalog); warnings for duplicates/external-ref via the preserved warnings payload with proceed semantics.
Ref generator: shared format-token module with T-020; sequence allocation SQL identical to the reference (single-transaction FOR UPDATE — R-3 compatible).
Breadth enforcement: leads.view_all-style permission decides whether list/detail queries filter to owned/assigned leads — implemented in the repository query, not post-filtering (P-03/P-08).
Owner defaulting: rm-slot role holders per T-020 assignments; region defaults from party when absent; priority derived High per high-value threshold business rule.
Bulk reassign: validates target assignee eligibility (rm-slot role), writes per-lead assignment change + one audit entry with the mandatory note per reference shape.
last_activity_at stamped on create and mutations (feeds inactivity job).

unit: Lead-ref format generation across templates/years; priority derivation from threshold; duplicate normalization
integration: Create: full validation catalog (each rule 422 with reference code); ref uniqueness under parallel creates (sequence transaction); status New; intake note becomes first activity
List: columns/filters/sort/paging/search parity; My-leads + breadth permission matrix (view_all sees all, restricted sees own/assigned only)
Bulk reassign: permission-bound, mandatory note enforced, audit written, assignments updated
Tenant isolation per endpoint; cross-tenant lead id 404
e2e: Lead intake + leads list specs adapted in T-043

findings.evaluator_ruling: RATIFIED 2026-07-19. Verified in the reference source first-hand: CreateLeadCommandHandler returns CreateLeadOutcomeDto.RequiresConfirmationFor BEFORE the transaction with nothing persisted, LeadEndpoints renders requiresConfirmation as Results.Json(..., 409), and createAnyway bypasses the gate. The measured reference wins over the task brief. Both behaviours (confirm-gate persists nothing; external-ref warning's row physically persists, on create AND edit) verified present in leads-core.test.ts:999-1123 and green.
findings.title: Task file contradicts the reference: duplicate-lead check is CONFIRM-GATED, not non-blocking
findings.detail: Task brief and implementation_details describe the duplicate-lead warning as non-blocking ('write and audit FIRST, search AFTER'). MEASURED: CreateLeadCommandHandler.cs:184-193 runs the duplicate check BEFORE the transaction and returns CreateLeadOutcomeDto.RequiresConfirmationFor with lead=null and nothing persisted; LeadEndpoints.cs:85-88 renders that as 409. The caller re-submits with createAnyway:true. AC-044's 'while still allowing creation to proceed' is satisfied by those proceed semantics. The genuinely non-blocking warnings are DUPLICATE_EXTERNAL_REF and DUPLICATE_PARTY_NAME, which ARE searched after the write. Implemented per the reference; both behaviours are tested, including that the confirm-gate persists nothing and that the external-ref warning's row physically persists.

findings.evaluator_ruling: RATIFIED 2026-07-19. Verified first-hand: LeadStore.FindOpenDuplicatesAsync is party_id + product_line_id + date window + open/quoted reporting categories, tenant-scoped, no name matching. Name normalization belongs to the party rule (T-023). Covering the lead rule at the integration level, where it is falsifiable, is the right call; no unit test for a rule that does not exist.
findings.title: Task file contradicts the reference: duplicate detection uses no name normalization
findings.detail: test_plan.unit asks for 'duplicate normalization'. MEASURED: the duplicate-LEAD rule is LeadStore.FindOpenDuplicatesAsync (:96-114) = same party_id + product_line_id + date_received within tenant duplicate_check_days + status reporting_category in (open,quoted). No names are involved. Name normalization/trigram similarity belongs to the PARTY duplicate rule (T-023). No such unit test was written; the lead rule is covered by integration tests instead, which is the level at which it is falsifiable.

findings.evaluator_ruling: VERIFIED, NOT CLOSED — remains ESCALATED TO THE HUMAN. The evaluator independently confirmed every load-bearing claim in the reference source: GetLeadQueryHandler.Handle calls only LeadStore.FindAsync, whose sole predicate is 'l.TenantId == tenantId && l.Id == id' (LeadStore.cs:49-52); the permission resolver is consulted in that handler ONLY to compute availableOperations, never to filter; ListLeadsQueryHandler alone resolves leads.view_all into the query filter. So the preserved contract for the detail GET is 200 within the tenant, and AC-045's '404/403 per the preserved contract' clause rests on a false premise. CONFIRMED this is breadth-WITHIN-tenant, not a tenant-isolation hole: the tenant predicate always applies, cross-tenant ids 404 identically to nonexistent ones (tested), and AC-021/AC-022 are fully satisfied. TECHNICAL RECOMMENDATION: option (a) — amend AC-045/V-058 (and the AC-042/V-055 defaulting clauses per F2) to match the preserved contract. Rationale: (i) the migration's stated goal is behaviour preservation, and the implementation matches the measured reference exactly; (ii) the surfaces that link to leads by id (dashboards drill, alerts, search, party leads card) are not breadth-filtered in the reference either, so tightening only the detail GET buys little real confidentiality — a restricted user still learns of leads through those surfaces — while 404ing links those surfaces legitimately produce; (iii) numeric sequential ids do make the open detail GET enumerable by a leads.view holder, so IF the business wants breadth to be a confidentiality boundary rather than a workload-scoping convenience, it must be applied consistently across detail GET, timeline (T-029), drill (T-035+), search, export (T-039) and the party leads card in ONE coordinated decision — that is a product change, not a T-024 bug, and piecemeal tightening here would produce an inconsistent and broken UX. If the human instead chooses option (b), the change is localised to getLeadById in service.ts plus one 404 test, as the implementor stated.
findings.title: OPEN DECISION for evaluator: GET /leads/{id} is NOT breadth-filtered in the reference
findings.detail: AC-045/V-058 say 'Direct GET of a lead outside the restricted caller's breadth -> 404/403 per the preserved contract'. MEASURED: GetLeadQueryHandler.cs:52-56 applies ONLY the tenant predicate via LeadStore.FindAsync; it does not consult leads.view_all or lead_assignments at all, so in the reference a leads.view holder CAN fetch any lead in their tenant by id. Only the LIST query applies breadth (ListLeadsQueryHandler.cs:28-35). Implemented AS MEASURED (detail GET returns 200) rather than silently tightening, because tightening would 404 leads that legitimately reach users via dashboards, alerts, search and party leads cards, all of which link by id. This is a genuine spec-vs-reference conflict with a security dimension: REQUESTING AN EVALUATOR RULING. If the ruling is to tighten, the change is localised to getLeadById in service.ts plus a breadth check, and a test should be added asserting 404 for an out-of-breadth id.
findings.resolution: Escalated to the human by the orchestrator and RULED 2026-07-19: amend the acceptance criteria to the preserved contract (option a, the evaluator's recommendation). AC-045 now states breadth is a LIST-query filter only and an out-of-breadth detail GET returns 200; V-058's negative test is inverted accordingly and now pins the behaviour FROM BOTH DIRECTIONS, plus a cross-tenant 404 case so tenant isolation - which IS the real confidentiality boundary - stays covered. AC-042/V-055 amended for the same false-premise class: owner and region are caller-required, not server-defaulted. NO CODE CHANGE; T-024 stands as implemented. The evaluator's caution is recorded for the record: if breadth ever should become a confidentiality boundary, it must be applied in ONE coordinated decision across detail, timeline, drill, search, export and the party leads card, since all of them surface the same leads by id.

findings.evaluator_ruling: CONFIRMED FIRST-HAND 2026-07-19 and ruled to need its OWN SMALL TASK (orchestrator to schedule; out of T-024 scope, correctly not fixed here). lib/validation's EXPLICIT_CODE is /^([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*)\|/, so the mixed-case FluentValidation-style prefixes verifiably present in brokers/schemas.ts, assignments/schemas.ts, api-access/schemas.ts:45 and business-rules/schemas.ts fall through: the code is DERIVED (which may or may not coincide with the intended prefix) and the literal 'NotNullValidator|' text leaks into the human-readable message the SPA displays. Cosmetic but repo-wide and user-visible. Follow-up task should either widen EXPLICIT_CODE to any pipe-prefixed token or restyle the sibling messages to SCREAMING_SNAKE codes, and add one regression test per affected domain asserting the rendered message carries no pipe prefix.
findings.title: Validation codes use SCREAMING_SNAKE explicit codes; sibling domains may leak a prefix
findings.detail: lib/validation/index.ts only recognises an explicit per-rule code when the message matches its EXPLICIT_CODE regex (leading capital, then capitals/digits/underscores, then a pipe). Mixed-case prefixes used elsewhere in the repo (e.g. 'NotNullValidator|...' in assignments/schemas.ts) do NOT match, so they fall through to the derived code AND leak the prefix text into the human-readable message. This domain therefore uses LEAD_* SCREAMING_SNAKE codes throughout, matching the validation module's own documented example (LEAD_DATE_RECEIVED_FUTURE). The sibling domains that use mixed-case prefixes look like a latent cosmetic defect -- REPORTED, deliberately NOT changed here (out of scope).
findings.summary: Validation codes use SCREAMING_SNAKE explicit codes;
